questions.text: As per the table below listing India's earliest designated Ramsar Sites (Wetlands of International Importance) and their designation dates, which wetland was the first to be designated in India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Pair elimination & Date check. India became a Ramsar signatory in 1981. The first two sites were designated on the same day: 01-10-1981. They are Chilika Lake (Odisha) and Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan). Conventionally, Chilika Lake is listed first in the official Ramsar Sites Information Service (RSIS) database for India (Site No. 229 vs 230). Wular (1990) and Sambhar (1990) came later. Step-by-step: On October 1, 1981, India designated its first two Ramsar sites: Chilika Lake (Ramsar Site No. 229) and Keoladeo Ghana (Ramsar Site No. 230). Since Chilika has the lower site number, it is technically the first entry.

questions.text: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, the definition of 'Wages' excludes specific components such as House Rent Allowance (HRA), Conveyance Allowance, Bonus, and Employer's PF contribution. However, the Code stipulates that if the total value of these exclusions exceeds a certain percentage of the total remuneration, the excess amount shall be deemed to be part of 'Wages'. What is this threshold percentage?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The definition clause (Section 2(y)) uses the phrase 'exceeds one-half' of the total remuneration. One-half equals 50%. Full Solution: As per Section 2(y) of the Code on Wages, 2019, 'wages' includes basic pay, dearness allowance, and retaining allowance, but excludes items like HRA, conveyance, overtime, bonus, PF, gratuity, etc. The Explanation to this clause explicitly states that if the sum of exclusions exceeds 50% (one-half) of the total remuneration, the amount exceeding 50% shall be added to wages for calculation purposes.
questions.topic: Code on Wages, 2019 - Definition of Wages

questions.text: A rectangular field has a length that is 25% more than its breadth. If the perimeter of the field is 120 meters, what is the area of the field in square meters? Use the approximation that 1.25x + x = 2.25x.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use Set Theory formula n(A∪B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A∩B). Total students = 60. Neither = 15 => At least one = 45. 45 = 30 + 40 - Both => Both = 70 - 45 = 25.

questions.text: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 360. If one of the numbers is 60, what is the other number?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the relation Product = HCF × LCM. The other number = (12 × 360) / 60 = 72. Full steps: Let the numbers be a and b. Given HCF = 12, LCM = 360, and a = 60. Since a × b = HCF × LCM, we have b = (12 × 360) / 60 = 4320 / 60 = 72.

questions.text: The 'Human Development Report' (HDR), which ranks countries based on the Human Development Index (HDI), is published annually by:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Keyword association. 'Development Programme' (UNDP) publishes 'Human Development Report'. World Bank publishes 'World Development Report'. IMF publishes 'World Economic Outlook'. WEF publishes 'Global Competitiveness Report' / 'Global Risks Report'. Full Solution: The Human Development Report is an independent publication commissioned by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). It was first launched in 1990 by the Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq. The World Bank's flagship report is the World Development Report.

questions.text: What was the code name of India's first nuclear test conducted at Pokhran, Rajasthan, in May 1974?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Year association. 1974 (Pokhran-I) = 'Smiling Buddha' (Peaceful Nuclear Explosion). 1998 (Pokhran-II) = 'Operation Shakti'. 'Operation Vijay' refers to Kargil War (1999) or Goa Liberation (1961). 'Operation Cactus' refers to Maldives intervention (1988). Full Solution: India's first nuclear test, conducted on 18 May 1974 at Pokhran, was codenamed 'Smiling Buddha' (or 'Pokhran-I'). The 1998 series of tests (Pokhran-II) were codenamed 'Operation Shakti'. Operation Vijay (1999) was the Kargil War. Operation Cactus (1988) was the Indian Armed Forces intervention in the Maldives.
questions.topic: Science & Technology / Modern History - Nuclear Programme

questions.text: In how many ways can 5 different books be arranged on a shelf such that two particular books are always together?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Treat the two particular books as a single unit. Then we have 4 units to arrange, giving 4! = 24 arrangements. The two books can be arranged internally in 2! = 2 ways. Total = 24 × 2 = 48. Full steps: Consider the two books as one combined entity. The 4 entities (combined entity + 3 other books) can be permuted in 4! = 24 ways. Within the combined entity, the two books can be ordered in 2! = 2 ways. By the multiplication principle, total arrangements = 24 × 2 = 48.

questions.text: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, what is the minimum number of employees required for an establishment to be compulsorily covered under the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) Scheme?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the 'EPF-20, ESI-10' mnemonic for the Code on Social Security, 2020 thresholds. Eliminate Option A (10) as it is the threshold for ESI coverage (Chapter IV). Eliminate Options B (15) and D (25) as they are not standard thresholds under any major labour code. Full Solution: As per Section 1(3) read with Chapter III (Employees' Provident Fund) of the Code on Social Security, 2020, the EPF Scheme applies compulsorily to every establishment in which 20 or more persons are employed. The threshold for Employees' State Insurance (ESI) under Chapter IV is 10 or more persons.
questions.topic: Code on Social Security, 2020 - Applicability Thresholds

questions.text: The Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced which significant feature in the provincial executive?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Match the feature to the correct Act timeline. Separate Electorates were introduced by the Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto). Provincial Autonomy and the Federal Court were introduced by the Government of India Act, 1935. Dyarchy (dual rule dividing subjects into Transferred and Reserved) was the specific hallmark of the 1919 Act. Worked Solution: The 1919 Act introduced Dyarchy in provinces where subjects were divided into 'Transferred' (administered by Governor with ministers) and 'Reserved' (administered by Governor and Executive Council), marking the first introduction of responsible government in a limited sphere.

questions.text: If the simple interest on a sum of money is 1/5th of the principal over a period of 2 years, what is the rate of interest per annum? A) 4% B) 5% C) 10% D) 12%
questions.solution: SHORTCUT: Use the formula SI = (P*R*T)/100. Since SI = P/5 and T=2, substitute directly: P/5 = (P*R*2)/100. Cancel P and solve R = 100/(5*2) = 10%. This avoids calculating specific principal values. FULL SOLUTION: Let Principal be P. Simple Interest = P/5. Time = 2 years. Using SI = (P * R * T) / 100, we get P/5 = (P * R * 2) / 100. Dividing both sides by P gives 1/5 = (2R)/100. Multiplying by 100 yields 20 = 2R, so R = 10%.

questions.text: Select the correct Indirect Speech form of the sentence: He said to me, "Please wait here till I return."

options.label: A
options.text: He requested me to wait there till he returned.

options.label: B
options.text: He requested me that I should wait here till he returns.

options.label: C
options.text: He asked me to wait here till he returned.

options.label: D
options.text: He told me to wait there until he returns.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options with 'here' (must change to 'there') and present tense 'returns' (must backshift to 'returned'). Option B retains 'here' and 'returns'. Option C retains 'here'. Option D uses 'told' (command) for 'please' (request) and keeps 'returns'. Option A correctly changes 'said to' -> 'requested', 'here' -> 'there', 'I' -> 'he', 'return' -> 'returned'. Worked Solution: 1. Reporting verb 'said to' with 'please' becomes 'requested'. 2. Pronoun 'I' changes to 'he' (subject of reporting verb). 3. Adverb 'here' changes to 'there'. 4. Tense backshift: Simple present 'return' becomes simple past 'returned'. 5. Imperative 'wait' becomes infinitive 'to wait'. Only Option A satisfies all rules.

questions.text: The Vernacular Press Act, 1878, enacted to control the Indian-language press, was passed during the viceroyalty of:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use chronological elimination. Lord Lytton (1876–1880) matches the year 1878. Lord Ripon (1880–1884) repealed it in 1882. Lord Dufferin (1884–1888) and Lord Curzon (1899–1905) served later. Full Solution: The Vernacular Press Act was enacted in 1878 by Lord Lytton. It was nicknamed the 'Gagging Act'. Lord Ripon, his successor, repealed it in 1882. Lord Curzon is associated with the Partition of Bengal (1905) and the Indian Universities Act (1904).

questions.text: How many trailing zeros are there in the decimal representation of 100! (100 factorial)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Number of trailing zeros in n! equals sum of floor(n/5^k). For 100: floor(100/5)=20, floor(100/25)=4, floor(100/125)=0 → total 24. Full: Each zero requires a factor 10 = 2×5; factors of 2 are abundant, so count factors of 5: 100/5=20, 100/25=4, sum=24.

questions.text: Select the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To fish in troubled waters'.

options.label: A
options.text: To catch fish during a storm

options.label: B
options.text: To take advantage of a chaotic situation for personal gain

options.label: C
options.text: To create trouble for others deliberately

questions.solution: Shortcut: Idioms are metaphorical; eliminate literal interpretations first. Options A and D describe physical acts of fishing/swimming, so they are incorrect. Option C describes creating trouble, but the idiom specifically means exploiting *existing* chaos. Option B captures the figurative meaning of profiting from disorder. Worked Solution: The phrase 'troubled waters' symbolizes a confused or unstable situation. 'Fishing' implies seeking something valuable (profit/advantage). Therefore, the idiom means trying to gain an advantage from a state of confusion or crisis.

questions.text: A company had 1,00,000 equity shares outstanding on 1st April 2023. On 1st October 2023, it issued 50,000 equity shares for cash. On 31st March 2024, the company issued bonus shares in the ratio of 1:1 (one bonus share for every one share held). The net profit for the year ended 31st March 2024 was ₹18,75,000. The net profit for the year ended 31st March 2023 was ₹10,00,000. What is the Basic EPS for the year ended 31st March 2024 and the restated Basic EPS for the year ended 31st March 2023?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Bonus issue adjustment factor = (Shares after bonus / Shares before bonus) = 2. Calculate Weighted Average Shares (WAS) before bonus for each year, multiply by 2, then divide profit by adjusted WAS. Step-by-step: 1. WAS 2023-24 (pre-bonus): (1,00,000 × 6/12) + (1,50,000 × 6/12) = 1,25,000 shares. 2. Adjusted WAS 2023-24 = 1,25,000 × 2 = 2,50,000 shares. Basic EPS 2024 = 18,75,000 / 2,50,000 = ₹7.50. 3. WAS 2022-23 (pre-bonus) = 1,00,000 shares. Adjusted WAS 2022-23 = 1,00,000 × 2 = 2,00,000 shares. Restated EPS 2023 = 10,00,000 / 2,00,000 = ₹5.00.

questions.text: The table below lists the year of establishment of five Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs). Which IIT was established earliest? Table:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Remember the historic order – Kharagpur (1951) is the first IIT. Full solution: From the table, IIT Kharagpur – 1951, IIT Bombay – 1958, IIT Madras – 1959, IIT Delhi – 1961. Hence the earliest is IIT Kharagpur (option index 2).

questions.text: A can complete a piece of work in 12 days and B can complete the same work in 18 days. They start working together but after 4 days A leaves. In how many days will B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Assume total work = LCM(12,18)=36 units. A does 3 units/day, B does 2 units/day. Together they do 5 units/day; in 4 days they complete 20 units, leaving 16 units. B finishes 16 units at 2 units/day in 8 days. Full steps: Work done in 4 days = 4*(1/12+1/18)=5/9. Remaining work = 4/9. B's one day work = 1/18. Days required = (4/9)/(1/18)=8 days.

questions.text: India's first dedicated polarimetry mission, XPoSat (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite), designed to study the polarization of intense X-ray sources, was successfully launched on which date using the PSLV-C58 rocket?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use temporal elimination of major ISRO launches. Sept 2, 2023 = Aditya-L1; Oct 21, 2023 = Gaganyaan TV-D1; Feb 2024 = INSAT-3DS (GSLV). XPoSat/PSLV-C58 is distinctively known as the 'New Year's Day' launch. Worked: XPoSat was launched on 1st January 2024 at 09:10 IST from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, aboard PSLV-C58, placing the satellite into a 650 km low Earth orbit.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error: 'The new manager is expected to plan, organize, and controlling the department.'
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check parallelism after 'to'. List requires bare infinitives: plan, organize, control. Option C uses gerund 'controlling'. Step-by-step: 1. Infinitive phrase 'to plan, organize, and control' requires parallel form. 2. 'Plan' and 'organize' are bare infinitives. 3. 'Controlling' is a gerund, breaking parallelism. 4. Correction: 'and control'.

questions.text: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock will the hands of a clock be at right angles to each other for the first time?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the formula |30H - 5.5M| = 90. For the first right angle between 4 and 5, the hour hand leads, so 30(4) - 5.5M = 90 → 120 - 5.5M = 90 → 5.5M = 30 → M = 60/11 = 5 5/11 minutes. Full Solution: At 4:00, the hour hand is at 120°. The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute on the hour hand. To form the first 90° angle, the minute hand must reduce the gap from 120° to 90°, i.e., cover 30° relatively. Time = Relative Distance / Relative Speed = 30° / 5.5° per min = 60/11 min = 5 5/11 min past 4.

questions.text: What is the remainder when 7^103 is divided by 24?
questions.solution: Shortcut: 7^2 = 49 ≡ 1 (mod 24). Therefore, 7^103 = 7 × (7^2)^51 ≡ 7 × 1^51 = 7 (mod 24). Full Solution: 7^2 = 49 = 24×2 + 1. So 7^103 = 7 × (49)^51 = 7 × (24×2 + 1)^51. Expanding by Binomial Theorem, every term contains a factor of 24 except the last term 7×1. Hence, the remainder is 7.

questions.text: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, what is the maximum monetary penalty that can be imposed for a significant data breach or non-compliance with the provisions of the Act?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate ₹5 Crore (limit under IT Act, 2000) and ₹500 Crore (often confused with Competition Act penalties). The DPDP Act, 2023 specifically caps the maximum penalty at ₹250 Crore in its Schedule. Worked Solution: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 prescribes penalties under Section 33 read with the Schedule. For contraventions such as failure to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach (Section 8(5)) or breach of obligations regarding children's data (Section 9), the maximum penalty is ₹250 crore per instance.

questions.text: What is the highest power of 5 that divides 50! (50 factorial) exactly?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use Legendre's formula (successive division by 5). 50/5 = 10, 10/5 = 2, 2/5 = 0. Sum of quotients = 10 + 2 = 12. Full Solution: The exponent of a prime p in n! is given by [n/p] + [n/p^2] + ... For p=5, n=50: [50/5] = 10, [50/25] = 2, [50/125] = 0. Total power = 10 + 2 = 12.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the highest peaks of major mountain ranges in Peninsular India, Anamudi (2,695 m), the highest peak in South India, is located in which state?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Range-State mapping. Anamudi is the highest peak of the Anamalai Hills (Western Ghats). Anamalai Hills are predominantly in Kerala (bordering TN). Doddabetta (2,637m) is the highest in Tamil Nadu (Nilgiris). Mullayanagiri (1,930m) is highest in Karnataka (Baba Budan Giri). Arma Konda (1,680m) is highest in Andhra Pradesh (Eastern Ghats). Step-by-step: Anamudi Peak is located in the Idukki district of Kerala, within the Eravikulam National Park. It is the highest point in India south of the Himalayas. The Anamalai range forms the border between Kerala and Tamil Nadu, but the summit lies in Kerala.

questions.text: The 'PM Vishwakarma' scheme, launched by the Prime Minister on the occasion of Vishwakarma Jayanti in September 2023, is a Central Sector Scheme designed to provide end-to-end support to which specific category of workers?

options.label: A
options.text: Small and marginal farmers for purchase of seeds and fertilizers

options.label: B
options.text: Traditional artisans and craftspeople engaged in handwork

options.label: C
options.text: Urban street vendors for affordable working capital loans

options.label: D
options.text: Women Self-Help Groups for micro-enterprise development

questions.solution: Shortcut (Scheme-Target Mapping): Option A describes PM-KISAN. Option C describes PM SVANidhi. Option D describes DAY-NRLM / Lakhpati Didi. The term 'Vishwakarma' (divine architect) directly signifies artisans/craftspeople. Step-by-step: Launched 17 Sept 2023. Targets 18 traditional trades (carpenter, blacksmith, potter, tailor, etc.). Provides recognition (Certificate/ID), skill upgradation (basic/advanced), toolkit incentive (Rs 15,000), collateral-free credit (up to Rs 3 lakh @ 5%), and digital transaction incentives.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the "Heart and Soul of the Constitution"?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Associate 'Heart and Soul' exclusively with Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) as termed by Dr. Ambedkar; eliminate Article 356 (President's Rule), Article 19 (Freedoms), and Article 21 (Life/Liberty) as they are rights/provisions protected by Article 32. Worked Solution: During Constituent Assembly debates on Draft Article 25 (now Article 32), Dr. B.R. Ambedkar explicitly stated it was the most important Article because it guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights, making other rights effective.

questions.text: The Quit India Movement (August Movement) was launched by the Indian National Congress under Mahatma Gandhi's leadership on which specific date?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate 26 January 1942 (pre-Cripps Mission) and 15 August 1942 (future Independence Day); the Quit India Resolution was passed by AICC on 8 August 1942 at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, launching the movement, while mass arrests occurred on 9 August. Worked Solution: The All India Congress Committee (AICC) met in Bombay on 7-8 August 1942 and ratified the 'Quit India Resolution' in the early hours of 8 August 1942. Mahatma Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' mantra on this day. The British responded by arresting the top leadership in the early hours of 9 August 1942 under Operation Zero Hour.

questions.text: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'At loggerheads'.
questions.solution: **Shortcut (Elimination by Tone/Context):** The word 'loggerheads' sounds heavy and clashing. Eliminate positive/neutral options: 'complete agreement' (A), 'working together' (D). 'State of confusion' (C) implies internal chaos, not interpersonal conflict. 'Strong disagreement' (B) fits the adversarial tone. **Step-by-Step:** 1. **Analyze the idiom:** 'At loggerheads' originates from a heavy tool/weapon or a blockhead, historically implying a violent dispute or deadlock. 2. **Evaluate Option A:** 'In complete agreement' is the antonym. Incorrect. 3. **Evaluate Option B:** 'In strong disagreement or dispute' matches the historical and current usage (e.g., 'The two ministers are at loggerheads over the policy'). Correct. 4. **Evaluate Option C:** 'In a state of confusion' describes a mental state, not a relational conflict. Incorrect. 5. **Evaluate Option D:** 'Working together harmoniously' is the opposite. Incorrect.

questions.text: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, what is the maximum age limit for a worker to be covered under the scheme for old-age pension and disability benefits?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compare with the EPFO definition. EPFO covers up to 59/60 usually, but the new Code extends this slightly or maintains the standard retirement age logic. Step-by-step: The Code on Social Security aims to provide benefits to workers in the unorganized sector and gig economy. For old age pension, the eligibility generally starts from a certain age (often 60 for men) and continues until death. However, the question asks for the *maximum* age to be covered or the age limit for entry? Re-reading standard syllabus: The Code provides benefits to workers up to the age of 60 for certain schemes, but specifically for old age pension, it is often 60 years. Let's check the specific phrasing in recent amendments. The Code extends coverage to gig workers and sets a retirement age context. The standard EPF covers up to 59 (now 60). The Social Security Code aims to cover workers up to age 60 for old age benefits. If the option is '60 years', that aligns with the new unified pension scheme logic replacing the older 59 limit.

questions.text: As per AS 2 (Valuation of Inventories), inventory is valued at the lower of Cost and Net Realisable Value (NRV) applied on an item-by-item basis. A company has three distinct inventory items with the following Cost and NRV: Item X: Cost ₹100, NRV ₹90 Item Y: Cost ₹200, NRV ₹220 Item Z: Cost ₹300, NRV ₹280 What is the total value of inventory to be recognised in the financial statements?
questions.solution: Shortcut: AS 2 mandates item-by-item valuation (lower of Cost/NRV per item), not aggregate comparison. Calculate lower value for each item first: X=min(100,90)=90; Y=min(200,220)=200; Z=min(300,280)=280. Sum = 570. Options A (600) and B (590) are traps using Total Cost and Total NRV respectively. Worked: Item X valued at ₹90 (NRV < Cost), Item Y at ₹200 (Cost < NRV), Item Z at ₹280 (NRV < Cost). Total recognised value = ₹90 + ₹200 + ₹280 = ₹570.
